note: Stage 3 zoned fill, measured in the dev build in the app's built-in browser pane (canvas 2048x1536, device pixel ratio 2). The pane was hidden, so requestAnimationFrame was replaced by a 16 ms timer to let the map load; every frame below was forced with map.redraw() and timed through gl.finish(), 40 frames per view, so the times are CPU plus GPU per frame and do not depend on the browser's frame pacing. Draw calls are counted on the shared WebGL context (MapLibre and the Three.js scene). GPU buffers: live bufferData bytes on that context. JS heap: performance.memory.usedJSHeapSize after the heap had settled (read every 7-8 s until stable), main thread only (MapLibre's workers are separate). Journey started, then paused (no haze or depth of field). Script: scripts/context/rome/measure-fill.js.

caveats: Single runs. GPU buffer totals include every tile the session had loaded, so they depend on the path the camera took; before and after followed the same path (start, pause, overview, regional, then the two-temples beat).
The regional view had no settled heap reading before; its unsettled readings swing by tens of megabytes with garbage collection and are left out.
A first version handed MapLibre the GeoJSON object, which it keeps a copy of on the main thread: about 70-80 MB more heap. The fill is now handed over as a blob URL, parsed in the worker.
